changesApplied.changeMade: Added JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable from Kubernetes secret 'metabob-rpc-api-secrets' key 'jwt-secret-key'
changesApplied.reason: Critical security fix: Injects strong random JWT secret (64-char hex) instead of weak default. Prevents token forgery attacks (OWASP A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures). Enables proper JWT token validation across all authentication flows.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: HIGH IMPACT - Affects all JWT token generation and validation. Changes propagate to: 1) Registration endpoint (token generation), 2) Login endpoint (token generation), 3) All protected endpoints (token validation), 4) Refresh token flow. Requires pod restart to take effect.
rippleEffects: All protected endpoints use SECRET_KEY for token validation

changesApplied.changeMade: Replaced naive result parsing (len(existing[0]) > 0) with robust 3-case structure analysis matching login endpoint pattern. Handles: 1) Official library format [{'status': 'OK', 'result': [...]}], 2) List of records [[{...}]], 3) Direct record format [{...}]
changesApplied.reason: Fixes false positive 'Email already registered' errors blocking user registration. Ensures consistent SurrealDB result parsing across authentication endpoints. Prevents registration denial for valid unique emails.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: MEDIUM IMPACT - Affects registration flow only. Enables new user onboarding. No breaking changes - only fixes bug. Changes propagate to: 1) Frontend registration form (will now succeed), 2) User creation in SurrealDB (will now execute), 3) Organization creation flow (will now complete).
changesApplied.beforeState: if existing and len(existing) > 0 and len(existing[0]) > 0: raise HTTPException
changesApplied.afterState: user_exists = False; if existing: parse structure (3 cases); if user_exists: raise HTTPException
rippleEffects: Frontend /cloud/register will now receive 200 OK instead of 400 Bad Request for unique emails
SurrealDB users table will populate with new user records
SurrealDB organizations table will populate with new org records
user_organizations junction table will link users to orgs

changesApplied.changeMade: Created Kubernetes secret with strong random JWT secret key (64-char hex, 32 bytes entropy)
changesApplied.reason: Provides secure storage for JWT signing key. Prevents secret exposure in deployment YAML. Follows Kubernetes secrets management best practices.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE - Secret is consumed by rpc-api deployment. Persists across pod restarts. Can be rotated without code changes by updating secret and restarting pods.
changesApplied.afterState: Secret 'metabob-rpc-api-secrets' created in namespace 'metabob' with key 'jwt-secret-key' containing 64-char hex string
rippleEffects: deployment-api.yaml references this secret via secretKeyRef
Pod environment includes JWT_SECRET_KEY from secret
jwt_auth.py reads strong secret instead of weak default

infrastructureChanges.command: kubectl create secret generic metabob-rpc-api-secrets -n metabob --from-literal=jwt-secret-key=$(openssl rand -hex 32)

deploymentRequired.reason: Deployment YAML changed, must be applied and pods restarted for JWT_SECRET_KEY to take effect

codeChangesCommitReady.commitMessage:
fix(auth): Add JWT_SECRET_KEY config and fix registration email check

- Add JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable to rpc-api deployment
- Create Kubernetes secret metabob-rpc-api-secrets with strong random key
- Fix registration endpoint email duplicate check with robust SurrealDB result parsing
- Match login endpoint's 3-case structure analysis pattern
- Fixes: Registration returns 400 'Email already registered' for all emails
- Fixes: JWT tokens use weak default secret causing security vulnerabilities

Impact:
- Registration flow now works for unique emails
- JWT tokens signed with cryptographically strong secret
- Consistent SurrealDB result parsing across auth endpoints

Refs: trace-dashboard-authentication-backend-fix

validationTests: Test 1: Verify JWT_SECRET_KEY in pod environment
Test 2: Test registration with unique email returns 200 OK
Test 3: Test login with registered user returns 200 OK with token
Test 4: Verify JWT token validation succeeds
